# Microsoft Copilot SDK > [!IMPORTANT] > **GitHub Copilot SDK is becoming Microsoft Copilot SDK**, the programmable interface for the Microsoft Copilot harness, the shared agent foundation used across Microsoft and GitHub products. > > The SDK repository will move to the Microsoft organization as part of a phased transition. Existing package names, namespaces, and some documentation may continue to reference GitHub Copilot SDK during the transition. **No immediate changes are required for existing users.** [Learn more about the transition](https://aka.ms/copilot-harness/announce). > > Support for the Copilot SDK remains the same. For more information: [SUPPORT.md](SUPPORT.md) Agents for every app. Embed Copilot's agentic workflows in your application with the Microsoft Copilot SDK for Python, TypeScript, Go, .NET, Java, and Rust. The Microsoft Copilot SDK exposes the same engine behind Copilot CLI: a production-tested agent runtime you can invoke programmatically. No need to build your own orchestration—you define agent behavior, Copilot handles planning, tool invocation, file edits, and more. ## Available SDKs | SDK | Location | Cookbook | Installation | API docs | | ------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | | **Node.js / TypeScript** | [`nodejs/`](./nodejs/) | [Cookbook](https://github.com/github/awesome-copilot/blob/main/cookbook/copilot-sdk/nodejs/README.md) | `npm install @microsoft/copilot-sdk` | | | **Python** | [`python/`](./python/) | [Cookbook](https://github.com/github/awesome-copilot/blob/main/cookbook/copilot-sdk/python/README.md) | `pip install microsoft-copilot-sdk` | | | **Go** | [`go/`](./go/) | [Cookbook](https://github.com/github/awesome-copilot/blob/main/cookbook/copilot-sdk/go/README.md) | `go get github.com/microsoft/copilot-sdk/go/v2` | [API docs](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/microsoft/copilot-sdk/go/v2#readme-api-reference) | | **.NET** | [`dotnet/`](./dotnet/) | [Cookbook](https://github.com/github/awesome-copilot/blob/main/cookbook/copilot-sdk/dotnet/README.md) | `dotnet add package Microsoft.Copilot.SDK` | | | **Rust** | [`rust/`](./rust/) | — | `cargo add copilot-sdk` | [API docs](https://docs.rs/copilot-sdk/latest/copilot_sdk/#api-reference) | | **Java** | [`java/`](./java/) | [Cookbook](https://github.com/github/awesome-copilot/blob/main/cookbook/copilot-sdk/java/README.md) | Maven coordinates
`com.microsoft:copilot-sdk`
See instructions for [Maven](./java/README.md#maven) and [Gradle](./java/README.md#gradle) | [API docs](https://javadoc.io/doc/com.microsoft/copilot-sdk/latest/) | See the individual SDK READMEs for installation, usage examples, and API reference. ## Getting Started For a complete walkthrough, see the **[Getting Started Guide](./docs/getting-started.md)**. Quick steps: 1. **(Optional) Install the Copilot CLI** A separate CLI installation is not required. Node.js and .NET include platform runtime artifacts, Python downloads them, and Rust bundles them with its default features. Go applications must run the bundler or provide a compatible runtime package; Java applications must add their platform runtime classifier. Follow the language README before starting a client. 2. **Install your preferred SDK** using the commands above. 3. **See the SDK README** for usage examples and API documentation. ## Architecture All SDKs drive the Copilot agent runtime over protocol-4 JSON-RPC. The runtime is a standalone component, separate from the Copilot CLI. By default, SDK v2 loads the native Rust runtime into your application through a C ABI and carries framed JSON-RPC messages over an in-memory connection. It does not embed a Node.js interpreter or start a separate runtime process: ``` Your Application ↓ SDK Client ↓ JSON-RPC (in memory, C ABI) Native Copilot runtime ``` The SDK manages its runtime host, but the native library remains loaded for the application process lifetime. In-process hosting provides neither crash isolation nor a sandbox. See [Run the Copilot runtime in process](./docs/setup/in-process-runtime.md) for requirements and v2 migration options. You can also run the runtime outside your application process: - **Spawned child process**: select a spawned stdio or TCP connection (`RuntimeConnection.forSpawnedStdio()` or `RuntimeConnection.forSpawnedTcp()` in TypeScript and Java; each SDK has an equivalent). The SDK starts the runtime as a child process and manages its lifecycle. Use it when you need crash isolation or per-client process configuration. - **Standalone runtime server**: run `copilot-runtime --server` yourself and attach to it over TCP with `RuntimeConnection.forTcp(host, port)`. One multi-tenant runtime server can serve many SDK clients and concurrent sessions. See [Connecting to a standalone runtime server](./docs/getting-started.md#connecting-to-a-standalone-runtime-server). ### Portable elicitation schemas For form elicitation callbacks, the portable schema contract is an object form with modeled `properties` and optional `required` fields (`type: "object"` on the wire; an SDK may represent the object type implicitly). Applications that support multiple SDK languages must use the modeled property definitions and must not depend on additional schema metadata (such as a top-level `title`) or on the insertion order of `properties`. Node.js and Rust pass through the wire schema, including additional metadata and property order. Python, Go, .NET, and Java reconstruct the callback schema from the modeled fields and do not offer that same preservation guarantee. Treat wire-schema preservation as a language-specific capability, not a cross-language requirement. ### Agent Finder Skill installation APIs Runtimes that grant `skill-confirmed-installation` expose `skills.planInstall`, `skills.applyInstall`, `skills.planUninstall`, `skills.applyUninstall`, `skills.installations.list/recover/status/cancel`, and `skills.installations.setEnabled`. Skill install reviews include the full verified `SKILL.md` content up to 256 KiB, catalogue identity, file manifest, and non-absolute personal target location. Summaries report `ownershipState`, `configuredEnabled`, `sessionState`, retained catalogue identity and `installedAt`. ## FAQ ### Do I need a GitHub Copilot subscription to use the SDK? Yes, a GitHub Copilot subscription is required to use the Microsoft Copilot SDK, **unless you are using BYOK (Bring Your Own Key)**. With BYOK, you can use the SDK without GitHub authentication by configuring your own API keys from supported LLM providers. For standard usage (non-BYOK), refer to the [GitHub Copilot pricing page](https://github.com/features/copilot#pricing), which includes a free tier with limited usage. ### How does billing work for SDK usage? Billing for the Microsoft Copilot SDK is based on the same model as the Copilot CLI, with each prompt being counted towards your usage allowance. For more information on Copilot usage billing, see [Usage in GitHub Copilot](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/reference/copilot-billing/models-and-pricing). ### Does it support BYOK (Bring Your Own Key)? Yes, the Microsoft Copilot SDK supports BYOK (Bring Your Own Key). You can configure the SDK to use your own API keys from supported LLM providers (e.g. OpenAI, Microsoft Foundry, Anthropic) to access models through those providers. See the **[BYOK documentation](./docs/auth/byok.md)** for setup instructions and examples. **Note:** BYOK uses key-based authentication only. Microsoft Entra ID (Azure AD), managed identities, and third-party identity providers are not supported. ### What authentication methods are supported? The SDK supports multiple authentication methods: - **GitHub signed-in user** - Uses stored OAuth credentials from `copilot` CLI login - **OAuth GitHub App** - Pass user tokens from your GitHub OAuth app - **Environment variables** - `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN`, `GH_TOKEN`, `GITHUB_TOKEN` - **BYOK** - Use your own API keys (no GitHub auth required) See the **[Authentication documentation](./docs/auth/README.md)** for details on each method. ### Do I need to install the Copilot CLI separately? No. The default needs a compatible native runtime, not a separately running CLI. Node.js, .NET, Python, and Rust provide acquisition or bundling; Go needs application-level bundling or an explicit runtime package, and Java needs the platform classifier dependency. Advanced: You can run a runtime binary you supply as a child process, or connect to a standalone runtime server. See the individual SDK README for language-specific options. ### What tools are enabled by default? By default, the SDK exposes the Copilot CLI's first-party tools, similar to running the CLI with `--allow-all`. Tool execution is still governed by each SDK's permission handler, so applications can approve, deny, or customize tool calls. releases.name: v2.0.2-preview.6
releases.body:
- Adds conversation and memory imports and UI snapshots; reuses owned file logging and secret filtering. Remote-host and CLI session plumbing remains internal.
- Preserves the final TCP shutdown response when an SDK-owned CLI exits first.
- Java stop() now preserves runtime shutdown rejection and timeout errors after cleanup.
- Disposing a pending AHP host cancels Mission Control enrollment without a shutdown timeout.
- Rust: Fixed a disconnect when macOS stops a live Copilot CLI process.

releases.name: v2.0.2-preview.5
releases.body:
- Reduce `session.shell.exec` launch overhead on supported Unix systems.
- Sandboxed extension providers can read linked sources and write to permitted extension folders while explicit filesystem restrictions and managed-policy changes remain enforced.
- Adds experimental semantic session and memory import APIs.
- Fixed MCP installation preparation for SDK sessions that supply an explicit GitHub token without a token provider.
- OpenTelemetry spans for MCP tool calls now report received RPC errors under `rpc.status_code` instead of `rpc.response.status_code`. Update queries that use the old key.
- OpenTelemetry `ahp.turn` spans now report cached input tokens under `gen_ai.usage.cache_read.input_tokens` instead of `gen_ai.usage.cache_read_tokens`. Update queries that use the old key.
- Background `model.*` events and model telemetry for compaction, session limits, and first tool calls still reach live SDK subscribers but are no longer saved in session history. Existing history is unchanged.
- Fixed an issue where an authenticated SDK client could receive a policy error when listing MCP installations after reconnecting, especially with telemetry disabled. Closing the original client

releases.name: v2.0.2-preview.4
releases.body:
- Node.js, Python, .NET, Rust, and Java SDK packages can now reach their registries even when the public source mirror is unavailable. The Go module and SDK GitHub release still require a verified public source snapshot.
- Add shared command operations and caller-specific settings through the SDK.
- `session.compaction_complete` now includes experimental `fusion` attribution when a HydraFusion turn compacts before its first phase.
- New `assistant.message` events no longer include the deprecated `encryptedContent` field. Read OpenAI Responses ciphertext from `reasoningBlocks.blocks` instead.
- Fixed an event ordering issue where `session.idle` could arrive before `assistant.idle` when a parent agent resumed after a background subagent completed.

releases.name: v2.0.2-preview.3
releases.body:
- Reduced telemetry and managed plugin overhead in SDK sessions, including sessions that use bring-your-own-key providers.
- SDK session events published while OpenTelemetry export is disabled are no longer exported if a later settings update enables export.
- Fixed a race during plugin initialization that could cause SDK session creation or resume to fail.
- `session.send` accepts `agentAuthored: true` for a message an agent wrote that the host delivers in the user role, such as an agent-created session's kickoff; automatic permission decisions then treat it as another agent's message, not the user's. Set it on the generated `session.send` request, or with `SendRequest::with_agent_authored` in Rust.
- The Copilot App can use the native Gemini Interactions API for supported Gemini models when the experiment is enabled.
- Cloud-task deletion supports an optional credential check before HTTP.
- Session teardown retires plugin work before its credential service closes.
- Session shutdown preserves the compaction start, cancellation result, and dispatched model.
- Session disposal rejects new background compaction, and lifecycle diagnostics omit rejected attempts.
- Background compacti

releases.name: v2.0.2-preview.2
releases.body:
- Fixed MCP prompt listing and retrieval, resource listing and reading, and resource template listing failing immediately after session creation with configured, enabled MCP servers. These calls now start the session's MCP servers without requiring a prior server-list call or user message.
- onErrorOccurred hooks now receive a failed model call's message as plain text instead of a JSON-quoted string.
- Fixed sandboxed Git operations on Windows with bin-only MinGit installations by allowing read-only access to default configuration, CA data, and templates while preserving sandbox restrictions.
- Sandboxed commands no longer start when a denied-path glob matches more than 100 paths; the error names the glob to narrow.
- Reduced slowdowns in long-running sessions where sub-agents execute many synchronous shell commands.
- Allow user.settings.loadForEdit to read a specified configuration directory and preserve object-shaped params for parameterless Go calls.
- Allow conditional user.settings.update calls to preserve concurrent settings changes, compare equivalent JSON numbers consistently, retain exact Go and Node settings integers, and accept Node negative-zero conditions.
- Keep Node

readmeHtml:
Microsoft Copilot SDK

Important

GitHub Copilot SDK is becoming Microsoft Copilot SDK, the programmable interface for the Microsoft Copilot harness, the shared agent foundation used across Microsoft and GitHub products.

The SDK repository will move to the Microsoft organization as part of a phased transition. Existing package names, namespaces, and some documentation may continue to reference GitHub Copilot SDK during the transition. No immediate changes are required for existing users. Learn more about the transition.

Support for the Copilot SDK remains the same. For more information: SUPPORT.md

Agents for every app.

Embed Copilot's agentic workflows in your application with the Microsoft Copilot SDK for Python, TypeScript, Go, .NET, Java, and Rust.

The Microsoft Copilot SDK exposes the same engine behind Copilot CLI: a production-tested agent runtime you can invoke programmatically. No need to build your own orchestration—you define agent behavior, Copilot handles planning, tool invocation, file edits, and more.

Available SDKs

SDK Location Cookbook Installation API docs
Node.js / TypeScript nodejs/ Cookbook npm install @microsoft/copilot-sdk
Python python/ Cookbook pip install microsoft-copilot-sdk
Go go/ Cookbook go get github.com/microsoft/copilot-sdk/go/v2 API docs
.NET dotnet/ Cookbook dotnet add package Microsoft.Copilot.SDK
Rust rust/ — cargo add copilot-sdk API docs
Java java/ Cookbook Maven coordinates
com.microsoft:copilot-sdk
See instructions for Maven and Gradle		 API docs

See the individual SDK READMEs for installation, usage examples, and API reference.

Getting Started

For a complete walkthrough, see the Getting Started Guide.

Quick steps:

  1. (Optional) Install the Copilot CLI

A separate CLI installation is not required. Node.js and .NET include platform runtime artifacts, Python downloads them, and Rust bundles them with its default features. Go applications must run the bundler or provide a compatible runtime package; Java applications must add their platform runtime classifier. Follow the language README before starting a client.

  1. Install your preferred SDK using the commands above.

  2. See the SDK README for usage examples and API documentation.

Architecture

All SDKs drive the Copilot agent runtime over protocol-4 JSON-RPC. The runtime is a standalone component, separate from the Copilot CLI. By default, SDK v2 loads the native Rust runtime into your application through a C ABI and carries framed JSON-RPC messages over an in-memory connection. It does not embed a Node.js interpreter or start a separate runtime process:

Your Application
       ↓
  SDK Client
       ↓ JSON-RPC (in memory, C ABI)
  Native Copilot runtime

The SDK manages its runtime host, but the native library remains loaded for the application process lifetime. In-process hosting provides neither crash isolation nor a sandbox. See Run the Copilot runtime in process for requirements and v2 migration options.

You can also run the runtime outside your application process:

  • Spawned child process: select a spawned stdio or TCP connection (RuntimeConnection.forSpawnedStdio() or RuntimeConnection.forSpawnedTcp() in TypeScript and Java; each SDK has an equivalent). The SDK starts the runtime as a child process and manages its lifecycle. Use it when you need crash isolation or per-client process configuration.
  • Standalone runtime server: run copilot-runtime --server yourself and attach to it over TCP with RuntimeConnection.forTcp(host, port). One multi-tenant runtime server can serve many SDK clients and concurrent sessions. See Connecting to a standalone runtime server.

Portable elicitation schemas

For form elicitation callbacks, the portable schema contract is an object form with modeled properties and optional required fields (type: "object" on the wire; an SDK may represent the object type implicitly). Applications that support multiple SDK languages must use the modeled property definitions and must not depend on additional schema metadata (such as a top-level title) or on the insertion order of properties.

Node.js and Rust pass through the wire schema, including additional metadata and property order. Python, Go, .NET, and Java reconstruct the callback schema from the modeled fields and do not offer that same preservation guarantee. Treat wire-schema preservation as a language-specific capability, not a cross-language requirement.

Agent Finder Skill installation APIs

Runtimes that grant skill-confirmed-installation expose skills.planInstall, skills.applyInstall, skills.planUninstall, skills.applyUninstall, skills.installations.list/recover/status/cancel, and skills.installations.setEnabled. Skill install reviews include the full verified SKILL.md content up to 256 KiB, catalogue identity, file manifest, and non-absolute personal target location. Summaries report ownershipState, configuredEnabled, sessionState, retained catalogue identity and installedAt.

FAQ

Do I need a GitHub Copilot subscription to use the SDK?

Yes, a GitHub Copilot subscription is required to use the Microsoft Copilot SDK, unless you are using BYOK (Bring Your Own Key). With BYOK, you can use the SDK without GitHub authentication by configuring your own API keys from supported LLM providers. For standard usage (non-BYOK), refer to the GitHub Copilot pricing page, which includes a free tier with limited usage.

How does billing work for SDK usage?

Billing for the Microsoft Copilot SDK is based on the same model as the Copilot CLI, with each prompt being counted towards your usage allowance. For more information on Copilot usage billing, see Usage in GitHub Copilot.

Does it support BYOK (Bring Your Own Key)?

Yes, the Microsoft Copilot SDK supports BYOK (Bring Your Own Key). You can configure the SDK to use your own API keys from supported LLM providers (e.g. OpenAI, Microsoft Foundry, Anthropic) to access models through those providers. See the BYOK documentation for setup instructions and examples.

Note: BYOK uses key-based authentication only. Microsoft Entra ID (Azure AD), managed identities, and third-party identity providers are not supported.

What authentication methods are supported?

The SDK supports multiple authentication methods:

  • GitHub signed-in user - Uses stored OAuth credentials from copilot CLI login
  • OAuth GitHub App - Pass user tokens from your GitHub OAuth app
  • Environment variables - COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN, GH_TOKEN, GITHUB_TOKEN
  • BYOK - Use your own API keys (no GitHub auth required)

See the Authentication documentation for details on each method.

Do I need to install the Copilot CLI separately?

No. The default needs a compatible native runtime, not a separately running CLI. Node.js, .NET, Python, and Rust provide acquisition or bundling; Go needs application-level bundling or an explicit runtime package, and Java needs the platform classifier dependency.

Advanced: You can run a runtime binary you supply as a child process, or connect to a standalone runtime server. See the individual SDK README for language-specific options.

What tools are enabled by default?

By default, the SDK exposes the Copilot CLI's first-party tools, similar to running the CLI with --allow-all. Tool execution is still governed by each SDK's permission handler, so applications can approve, deny, or customize tool calls. You can customize tool availability by configuring the SDK client options to enable and disable specific tools. Refer to the individual SDK documentation for details on tool configuration and to the Copilot CLI documentation for the list of available tools.

Can I use custom agents, skills or tools?

Yes, the Microsoft Copilot SDK allows you to define custom agents, skills, and tools. You can extend the functionality of the agents by implementing your own logic and integrating additional tools as needed. Refer to the SDK documentation of your preferred language for more details.

Are there instructions or SDK guidance for Copilot to speed up development?

Yes, check out the custom instructions and SDK-specific guidance:

  • Node.js / TypeScript
  • Python
  • .NET
  • Go
  • Rust (SDK guidance; custom instructions not yet published)
  • Java

What models are supported?

All models available via Copilot CLI are supported in the SDK. The SDK also exposes a method which will return the models available so they can be accessed at runtime.

Is the SDK production-ready?

The Microsoft Copilot SDK is generally available and follows semantic versioning. See CHANGELOG.md for release notes.

How do I report issues or request features?

Please use the GitHub Issues page to report bugs or request new features. We welcome your feedback to help improve the SDK.

  • Setup Guides – Architecture, deployment, and scaling

aiSummary.oneLiner: The official multi-language SDK for integrating GitHub Copilot's AI capabilities natively into your own applications.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: The GitHub Copilot SDK provides an official programming interface to Copilot's AI services across multiple languages including Node.js, Python, Go, .NET, Rust, and Java. Rather than building raw HTTP clients to interact with LLMs, developers use this SDK to communicate with a local JSON-RPC server (the Copilot CLI), which handles authentication, routing, and tool execution. It abstracts away the complexity of managing LLM connections, supports defining custom agents and skills, and enables developers to extend Copilot's functionality using their own logic. Notably, it also supports a 'Bring Your Own Key' (BYOK) mode, allowing users to leverage supported models without a GitHub subscription.
keyFeatures: JSON-RPC server architecture: Communicates with a bundled or external Copilot CLI server to handle low-level LLM interactions securely.
Multi-language support: Provides official, idiomatic libraries for Node.js, Python, Go, .NET, Rust, and Java.
Bring Your Own Key (BYOK): Allows bypassing GitHub authentication by plugging in direct API keys for providers like OpenAI or Anthropic.
Custom agents and tools: Enables developers to define their own logic, tools, and skills to extend the base Copilot capabilities.
Built-in authentication: Natively handles GitHub OAuth tokens and environment variables without requiring manual token refresh logic.

useCases.description: DevOps teams build CI/CD bots using the Python SDK that automatically analyze pull requests using Copilot's underlying models.

useCases.title: Internal CLI tools
useCases.description: Platform engineers use the Go SDK to build interactive terminal assistants that understand their company's proprietary infrastructure.

useCases.title: Provider-agnostic AI apps
useCases.description: Startups leverage the BYOK feature to prototype AI applications using OpenAI keys while maintaining compatibility with the Copilot ecosystem.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: This SDK is designed for software developers and enterprise teams looking to build custom, AI-powered developer tools, plugins, or automated agents backed by GitHub Copilot's infrastructure and models. It requires proficiency in integrating GitHub Copilot extensions into developer tools.
